answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using latency trilateration. Fixed beacons emit a verification pulse, measuring light-speed propagation delays to anchor each agent to a verified physical location. Attackers incur the scarce cost of maintaining separate hardware transceivers across distinct real estate, from willow valleys to rocky karst terrain, preventing zero-cost virtualization. However, signal multipath interference can distort timing and erroneously reject honest nodes.
